results.title: Mądrość jako przedmiot zarządzania

abstracts.content: Ze względu na globalne problemy społeczne oraz wraz z rozwojem koncepcji zarządzania wiedzą mądrość staje się centralną kategorią rozważań i wiodącym punktem odniesienia w ramach wielu obszarów eksploracji. Mimo tego nadal jest pojęciem wieloznacznym, raczej o znamionach teoretycznego konstruktu. Stała się terminem referencyjnym dla kilku współczesnych nurtów myślenia i wymaga szczegółowych analiz. Celem opracowania jest rozpoznanie pojęcia mądrość w perspektywie nauk o zarządzaniu i jakości, identyfikacja jej komponentów oraz wskazanie ich wzajemnych współzależności. Eksploracje zostały zrealizowane, w ramach podejścia dedukcyjnego, przy zastosowaniu krytycznego przeglądu literatury. Mądrość najczęściej wyłania się jako obiekt zarządzania i w perspektywie nauk o zarządzaniu i jakości jest postrzegana zarówno w ujęciu atrybutowym, jak i czynnościowym oraz rzeczowym. Jej źródłem jest głównie wiedza spersonalizowana i cicha, zakorzeniona w człowieku posiadającym intelekt, będącym katalizatorem i kontekstem do przekształcania wiedzy w mądrość, warunkującą mądre i zhumanizowane działanie. Emanacją mądrości jest umiejętność wyboru właściwego działania w oparciu o odpowiednią wiedzę i wspólnie wyznawane oraz powszechnie akceptowane wartości, ukierunkowanego na osiągnięcie dobra własnego i innych przy świadomości, że osobiste działania mają konsekwencje społeczne. Taka interpretacja łączy większość aktualnych poglądów zawartych w formatach humanizing strategy, people-centered orientation czy knowmad i knowledge-intensive society wpisujących się w charakterystykę Społeczeństwa 5.0. (abstrakt oryginalny)

Due to global social problems and with the development of the concept of knowledge management, wisdom is becoming a central category of considerations and a leading point of reference in many areas of exploration. Despite this, it is still an ambiguous concept, rather a theoretical construct. It has become a reference term for several contemporary trends in thought and requires detailed analysis. The aim of the study is to recognize the concept of wisdom from the perspective of management and quality sciences, identify its components and indicate their mutual interdependencies. The exploration was carried out in a deductive approach using a critical literature review. Wisdom most often emerges as an object of management and, from the perspective of management and quality sciences, it is perceived both in terms of attributes, activities and aptitudes. Its source is mainly personalized and tacit knowledge, rooted in a person with intellect, which is a catalyst and context for transforming knowledge into wisdom, conditioning wise and human-oriented actions. An emanation of wisdom is the ability to choose the right action based on appropriate knowledge and shared and generally accepted values, aimed at achieving the good of oneself and others, while being aware that personal actions have social consequences. This interpretation combines most of the current views contained in the formats of humanizing strategy, people-centered orientation or knowmad and knowledge-intensive society, which fit the characteristics of Society 5.0. (original abstract)

results.title: Socio-Demographic Influences on Dietary Habits and Nutritional Awareness : a Case Study of Polish Biathlon Association National Team Members

abstracts.content: Introduction: This study investigated the influence of sociodemographic factors on the dietary habits of athletes of the Polish Biathlon Association. Focusing on age, education, employment status, and gender, this research assesses food choices, meal preparation, and nutritional awareness within a structured sports environment. A cross-sectional survey of 54 athletes was conducted using a modified "Eating Habits of Poles" questionnaire to explore food selection, preparation methods, consumption patterns, and nutritional perspectives. This focus on biathletes emphasizes their distinct dietary needs, which arise from the demanding combination of endurance and precision in their sport, providing valuable insights for tailored dietary strategies to enhance their performance and overall health. Results: The results indicate that age, education, and employment status significantly influence Polish biathletes' dietary habits and nutritional awareness. Older athletes (under 23 years) demonstrated significantly higher nutritional awareness regarding modern dietary trends (p = 0.015). In contrast, 50% of higher-education athletes were more engaged in meal planning and healthier food choices than those with elementary education (p = 0.031). Employment status also played a role; 70% of the athletes were students who exhibited more convenience-based food choices, whereas 30% were employed and maintained more structured eating patterns (p = 0.008). Minimal gender differences were found, with 50% of male and 50% of female athletes showing similar dietary habits, likely due to standardized nutrition programs provided to all athletes. Conclusions: This indicates a potential need for further research to determine whether professional dietary support can effectively address typical gender-related variations in food behavior and lead to improvements in dietary outcomes. This study highlights the importance of targeted nutrition education and professional support for optimizing the nutritional habits of professional athletes. This emphasizes that socio-demographic factors such as age, education, and employment status significantly shape these behaviors, underscoring the need for personalized nutritional strategies within athletic programs. (original abstract)

results.title: Women Leaders in Logistics for the Economy 5.0

abstracts.content: The complexity of the technologized socioeconomic reality poses a number of challenges for today's managers. Many times their actions are a test of their leadership. A particularly interesting area of research in this regard is the logistics sector, which so far has been regarded as typically male and which has been undergoing a transformation in favor of an increasing representation of women for some years now. The authors sought to answer questions such as: what qualities, skills and competences will enable women working in logistics to pursue their careers and achieve their goals in the face of the challenges of a 5.0 economy. The aim of the article is to identify those leadership skills and competences of women in logistics that predispose them to lead on their way to business success in enterprises. In the research process, mixed research methodologies were used, combining the results of secondary source analysis obtained from Scopus and Web of Science databases with information obtained from a quantitative survey based on the CAWI diagnostic survey method. The analyses resulted in a model of an exemplary image combining traits, skills and competencies, as well as attributes of effectiveness, which may be helpful for women in shaping their leadership position in the management structures of companies in the logistics industry. The resulting material complements the existing body of research on the role and importance of women in business including, in particular, the inclusion of women in logistics. The main strength of the work is to identify areas that women should improve in order to increase their participation in managerial positions in the logistics industry. (original abstract)

Factors shaping environmental awareness of young adults and its importance in market decision-making processes

abstracts.content:
Objective: This study aims to present the results of the analysis of factors influencing the ecological awareness of young adults and their importance in market decision-making. 
 Research Design & Methods: The study utilized an online survey sheet that constituted the basis for the conclusions. The survey covered selected students of two universities in Krakow who completed 540 questionnaires. We applied cross-tabulation analysis in various cross-sections was applied using Pearson's chi-square statistics, contingency coefficient, and Cramer's V coefficient. We based the analysis on the declarations of young adults about their selected behaviours that significantly impact the state of the natural environment and, at the same time, require organisational and/or financial commitment from them. 
 Findings: We established that the surveyed young adults had a relatively high awareness of the importance of pro-environmental behaviour for the general climate situation in the world and the related well-being of humanity. At the level of description of the surrounding reality, the responses included both concern for the planet's future and fear of the deterioration of the climate situation. At the same time, the young adults were not ready to increase their involvement in pro-environmental activities. They declared a lack of interest in the possibility of financial support for broadly perceived ecological activities. Pro-environmental aspects are not crucial for them in purchasing or employment decisions. The basic forms of commitment to the environment are promotional campaigns which they occasionally join, such as collecting plastic bottle caps. 
 Implications & Recommendations: Similarly to the research results described as part of the literature review, the results show that to increase the involvement of young adults in pro-environmental activities, they need to be offered simple activities that do not require their financial involvement. A further increase in involvement will only be possible after the implementation of further educational campaigns. 
 Contribution & Value Added: Further research proposed a generalised linear model (GLZ) that helped describe the relationship between market decisions made by young adults and their demographic characteristics. We considered the variable containing answers to the question 'Are your purchasing decisions influenced by the environmental orientation of the producers of the goods you buy?' as the dependent variable. The obtained research and analysis results allowed for evaluating the answers to the question about the respondents' gender and form of studies to be dependent variables. (original abstract)

results.title: Koncepcja oceny przedsiębiorczości publicznej w urzędach administracji samorządowej

abstracts.content: Enhancing the public sector's efficiency and effectiveness is currently a widely explored area in management and quality Sciences, both in Poland and worldwide. With stakeholder demands growing, the pressure is constant to increase both the rangę and ąuality of public services, while at the same time optimising hudgets. Amid such demands, developing an optimal way to achieve increasingly diverse goals, complex needs, and social problems is of paramount importance. Concerning public entrepreneurship in local government offices, this dissertation examines efforts made by relatively autonomous units, such as local government offices, to increase management efficiency and implement various mechanisms to generale value for stakeholders. A number of foreign studies, both theoretical and practical, have highlighted the concept of public entrepreneurship. These have become the basis for exploring manifestations of this form of entrepreneurship in Poland as well. A thorough examination of Polish local government offices has been identified as a gap to be filled in the research. As the multidimensionality and diverse aspects of understanding public entrepreneurship have been highlighted in the literature, there is a recognised need to develop a model for measuring public entrepreneurship, one that takes into account the specificities of the public sector. Diagnosing and assessing public entrepreneurship in local government offices at the municipal level should broaden the perspective on entrepreneurship in the public sector. Such efforts are associated with the development of public management as a sub-discipline of management and ąuality Sciences. This dissertation identifies components of public entrepreneurship in local government offices in Poland, including proactive actions, innovation, and risk-taking in the public sector. It contributes to the knowledge on the methodological aspects of public entrepreneurship. The main aim of this study is to create a methodological basis for evaluating the public entrepreneurship in local government offices in Poland, taking into account the specificity of the public sector. Chapter One examines the characteristics of entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship in selected fields of social Sciences. It demonstrates the importance of entrepreneurship in the economy, emphasising the diversity of interpretations of this concept in the development of various scientific disciplines. The chapter also presents the genesis and development of entrepreneurship in the theory of economics and finance, the essence of entrepreneurship in management and ąuality Sciences, and sociological and psychological perspectives on entrepreneurship. Finally, it discusses research on entrepreneurship, accentuating the multi-aspect nature of the issue. Chapter Two explores the management of public sector entities, including its evolution and the main concepts it involves: Weberian public administration, New Public Management, public governance, the theory of the neo-Weberian state, and Digital Era Governance. It also focuses on the premises and relationships between entrepreneurship and management concepts in the public sector. Chapter Three discusses the essence and assumptions of public entrepreneurship. It begins with a systematic review of the literature on the development of research on public entrepreneurship in Poland and globally. It systematises the concept and characteristics of the public entrepreneur across different disciplines: economics, management, public administration, and political science. It then looks at organisational entrepreneurship as a basis for interpreting public entrepreneurship. This characterisation lays the groundwork for the premises and genesis of entrepreneurship in the public sector and explains an entrepreneurial orientation in the conceptualising the measurement of public entrepreneurship. The chapter also includes reviews of models for measuring public entrepreneurship. Chapter Four presents the determinants of entrepreneurship in local government offices. It begins with an outline of local government administration in Poland, and an explanation of the concept of local government and administrative offices. It then presents the uniąue features of public sector management, focusing on the diversity of the environment, characteristics and determinants of organisational culture in the public sector, institutional isomorphism, and its translation into organisational development in this sector. Additionally, the chapter discusses the conditions and systematisation of innovation and the concept of public value through the prism of assessing the effectiveness of the public sector. It also discusses digital transformation in the public sector. Chapter Five presents the methodological foundations for evaluating public entrepreneurship in local government offices at the municipal level. It first puts forward the assumptions and procedures of research on evaluating public entrepreneurship in local government offices at the municipal level through the prism of the distinctive phases of research proceedings and types of validation. It then presents a review of revisions of previous research on public entrepreneurship. These studies helped identify a cognitive, methodological, and practical gaps in the knowledge base, formulate the research problem, and establish the general and specific objectives of the dissertation. The operationalisation phase presents the model for assessing public entrepreneurship in local government offices at the municipal level, the main hypotheses and specific hypotheses, the methods for testing the hypotheses and measurement tools for variables, and the research tool model. The verification phase presents an initial assessment of the assumptions, an evaluation of the structure of the research model, and verification of its correctness. The measurement and inference phase also characterises the research sample and the empirical research. Chapter Six presents field research and a discussion of the results, which were subjected to multi-aspect analysis using statistical methods. On this basis, the level of public entrepreneurship in the local government offices surveyed at the municipal level in Poland was assessed. The chapter also examines the determinants of entrepreneurship in the offices surveyed, assesses the formation of public value for stakeholders in the offices, evaluates the research model and verifies the research hypotheses. It concludes with a discussion of the research results. The finał chapter presents conclusions from the research, theoretical and practical implications, limitations and further research directions, as well as recommendations and suggestions for academics and practitioners interested in management in local government offices at the municipal level in Poland. (original abstract)

abstracts.content: Z transferem technologii wiąże się przyjmowanie i upowszechnianie rozwiązań innowacyjnych. To nie samo odkrywanie nowej wiedzy prowadzi do postępu gospodarczego. Aby osiągnąć korzyści biznesowe i społeczne, konieczne jest wdrożenie innowacji przez przedsiębiorstwa. W konsekwencji, jeśli innowacja nie jest wdrażana bezpośrednio przez innowatora, może zostać przetransferowana do innych podmiotów np. w drodze umów licencyjnych lub upowszechniona np. w sieci transferu technologii. Skuteczne przeprowadzenie procesu transferu technologii nabiera strategicznego znaczenia w realiach przyspieszonej transformacji procesów społeczno-gospodarczych spowodowanej dynamicznym rozwojem technologicznym. Przedmiotem rozważań jest asymetryczna informacja, która stwarza brokerom technologii warunki do poszukiwania nowych możliwości biznesowych dla uczestników sieci transferu technologii. (abstrakt oryginalny)

Related to technology transfer is the issue of adopting and/or disseminating innovative solutions. It is not the discovery of new knowledge alone that leads to economic progress. To achieve business and/or social benefits, it is necessary for companies to implement the innovation. Consequently, if the innovation is not implemented directly by the innovator, it must be transferred to other entities, for example, through licensing agreements or disseminated, for example, in a technology transfer network. The effective execution of the technology transfer process acquires strategic importance in the reality of accelerated transformation of socio-economic processes caused by dynamic technological development. The subject of consideration is asymmetric information, which creates conditions for technology brokers to seek new business opportunities for technology transfer network participants. (original abstract)

results.title: Celecoxib for Mood Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstracts.content: The effects of celecoxib on a broad spectrum of mood disorders and on inflammatory parameters have not yet been comprehensively evaluated. The aim of this study was to systematically summarize the available knowledge on this topic. Data from both preclinical and clinical studies were analyzed, considering the efficacy and safety of celecoxib in the treatment of mood disorders, as well as the correlation of inflammatory parameters with the effect of celecoxib treatment. Forty-four studies were included. We found evidence supporting the antidepressant efficacy of celecoxib in a dose of 400 mg/day used for 6 weeks as an add-on treatment in major depression (SMD = −1.12 [95%Cl: −1.71,−0.52], p = 0.0002) and mania (SMD = −0.82 [95% CI:−1.62,−0.01], p = 0.05). The antidepressant efficacy of celecoxib in the above dosage used as sole treatment was also confirmed in depressed patients with somatic comorbidity (SMD = −1.35 [95% CI:−1.95,−0.75], p < 0.0001). We found no conclusive evidence for the effectiveness of celecoxib in bipolar depression. Celecoxib at a dose of 400 mg/d used for up to 12 weeks appeared to be a safe treatment in patients with mood disorders. Although an association between celecoxib response and inflammatory parameters has been found in preclinical studies, this has not been confirmed in clinical trials. Further studies are needed to evaluate the efficacy of celecoxib in bipolar depression, as well as long-term studies evaluating the safety and efficacy of celecoxib in recurrent mood disorders, studies involving treatment-resistant populations, and assessing the association of celecoxib treatment with inflammatory markers.

Purpose: The purpose of the article is to characterize the possibilities of using artificial intelligence in relation to food safety in the food chain. 
Design/methodology/approach: A review of recent literature on AI in the food industry was conducted in relation to food safety. 
Findings/conclusions: AI is used in processes in the food chain concerning its various participants (farmers, producers, distributors) as a preventive measure against food safety hazards and threats, as well as in the event of a food safety hazard and threat. AI gives the ability to collect, process, model and analyze large amounts of data, which is why its applications in the food industry and ensuring food safety are very wide - from monitoring, risk prediction, prevention, training, to quick reactions related to product withdrawal from the market and informing institutions and consumers. 
Research limitations: Theoretical aspects have been addressed, but they can be expanded to include practical aspects, opinions of consumers, producers and institutions. 
Practical implications: The article points to the important issue of the use of AI in quality assurance, in terms of prevention, but also in response to threats arising from food. AI can be used in various areas. We must remember ethics and responsibility when using AI. 
Originality/value: This is a current topic related to the development of AI, its advantages and the threats it brings. (original abstract)

results.title: Korzyści ekonomiczne zagospodarowania wód opadowych w mieście

abstracts.content: W jakich obszarach ekonomia zajmuje się wodą? Co tworzy wartość ekonomiczną wody? Jakim dobrem publicznym jest woda? Pytania te stały się podstawą rozważań teoretycznych, które następnie zawężono do analiz wód opadowych i roztopowych. Dalsze pytania dotyczą korzyści płynących z zagospodarowania wód opadowych w mieście oraz możliwych oszczędności ekonomicznych uzyskanych dzięki wdrożeniu niebiesko-zielonej infrastruktury i rozwiązań opartych na przyrodzie. Celem badawczym monografii jest opracowanie metodyki obliczania korzyści ekonomicznych z zagospodarowania wód opadowych i roztopowych w mieście, z uwzględnieniem podmiotów zaangażowanych w ten proces. W całej monografii przyjęto zasadę "od ogółu do szczegółu", gdyż trudno byłoby dyskutować o wodach opadowych bez odniesienia się do bardziej ogólnych badań nad wodą jako zasobem lub dobrem w naukach ekonomicznych. Chociaż ekonomia zajmuje się szeroko kwestią zasobów naturalnych, znalezienie rozważań i badań dotyczących wody, zwłaszcza wody deszczowej, było trudne. Co więcej, analizy wód opadowych prowadzono dopiero od dwóch dekad, a większość prac dotyczyła praktycznych metod zagospodarowania wód opadowych. Jednakże w ostatnich latach zaczęły pojawiać się badania naukowe dotyczące korzyści płynących z zagospodarowania wód opadowych (jako możliwości szybkiego ich odprowadzenia do odbiornika). W niniejszej monografii przedstawiono wybrane podejścia do analizy korzyści wynikających z zagospodarowania wód opadowych i roztopowych w miastach. Proponuje także szczegółową metodykę wyliczania tych świadczeń w Polsce. Monografia składa się z pięciu rozdziałów. (fragment tekstu)

In which areas does economics deal with water? What creates the economic value of water? What kind of public good is water? These ąuestions became the basis for theoretical considerations, which were then narrowed down to analyses of rainwater and snowmelt. Further ąuestions concern the benefits of rainwater management in the city and possible economic savings achieved thanks to implementing blue-green infrastructure and nature-based Solutions. The research objective of the monograph is to devełop a methodology for calculating the economic benefits of rainwater and meltwater management in the city, taking into account the entities involved in the process. A "from generał to specific" principal is adopted throughout the monograph as it would be difficult to argue about rainwater without referring to morę generał research on water as a resource or as a good in economic Sciences. Although economics deals extensively with the issue of natural resources, water-, especially rainwater-oriented, considerations and studies have been challenging to find. Moreover, analyses of rainwater have been done only in the last two decades, with much of the work examining practical methods of rainwater management. However, scientific studies on the benefits of rainwater management (as an option to its ąuick discharge to the receiver) have begun to appear in the past few years. This monograph presents selected approaches to analysing the benefits of rainwater and meltwater management in cities. It also proposes a detailed methodology for calculating these benefits in Poland. The monograph comprises five chapters. The first presents a review of the economics literaturę on water, incłuding rainwater. It covers natural resources in economic Sciences, including water, and then morę specifically the issues of water ownership and access systems, water as a public good, and how the perception of water as a public, private, club or common good differ. It addresses the issue of the value of water, including the difference between value and price, as well as total economic value and its components, including in relation to water. The iSsues of water ownership, water law and rights to water are not discussed in the monograph due to the limited size of the publication. However, these issues have been addressed elsewhere and should be treated as supplementary to the present considerations on the importance of water in economics. The second chapter examines environmental benefits and costs from several perspectives, including the development of these categories in economics, their practical application in the framework of a Cost-Benefit Analysis methodology, the approach presented in the Water Framework Directive and in the methodology of ecosystem services analysis. This is a comprehensive approach to the subject of economic benefits and costs. Each case addresses water issues. Chapter Three focuses on the benefits (and costs) of rainwater and snowmelt management in the city. It presents an integrated approach to water management in the city and its advantages as well as stages of cities' evolution in this matter. It also describes the benefits of introducing biue-green infrastructure in the city and the dilemmas it brings about. Finally, it proposes an original model approach to valorising the benefits of rainwater and meltwater management in the city. The further part of the monograph develops this approach and evaluates it in relation to economic benefits. Chapter Four examines how rainwater is managed in Polish cities, the intensification of problems connected with flash flooding in urban areas and actions taken at the strategie and local level in Poland to counteract their negative effeets. It describes and maps Poland's rainwater management system, and identifies and unifies the description of three basie models of rainwater and snowmelt management developed in Polish cities. Chapter Five looks at the results of empirical research conducted by the author and presented using the example of a selected city. This chapter presents a new methodical approach to identifying the benefits of modifying a rainwater management system as well as calculations of benefits in the accounting of various entities involved in this process (the entities are identified in Chapter Four). The author estimates some valuation items with caution and strict assumptions, while also admitting that there are areas where a change in the way data is collected or digitised is reąuired or that data collecting needs to start to enable wider estimation. These findings also carry significant cognitive value and are every bit as important as the results from the areas that have been valorised. The chapter ends with a discussion on the results obtained and with recommended meas- ures that should be implemented in Poland. It should be emphasised that due to the specificity of rainwater and snowmelt water management, inspirations from other countries, especially from other climatic zones, cannot always be transferred to Poland. That is not to say that such sources should not be analysed, nor that local or regional Solutions and changes should not be considered. In this monograph, the author has sought to combine extreme poles: economic theories regarding natural resources, including water, with practical activities related to rainwater, universal methods of valorising economic benefits with the practice of Polish cities operating within a specific legał, administrative and economic reality. The author hopes that this monograph lays the groundwork for bridges to be built between these extremes and that it will be a useful publication for a wide group of scientists, practitioners and activists interested in the economic benefits of rainwater and snowmelt management in cities, as well as students of both environmental engineering and economics. (original abstract)

Understanding Customer Needs in Shaping Socially Responsible Enterprises in Inter-organizational Networks

journal.title: Zeszyty Naukowe Politechniki Śląskiej. Seria Organizacja i Zarządzanie

abstracts.content:
Purpose: The aim of the study is to understand the relationship between aligning with customer needs in the context of shaping corporate social responsibility for companies operating in inter organizational networks and the benefits of improved access to market information, strengthening market position, and increasing the flexibility of business operations as advantages gained from mutual connections and relationships with market partners.
 Design/methodology/approach: Based on literature studies and statistical analysis using the Kendall rank correlation and Kruskal-Wallis test, we analyze the relationship between adapting to customer needs and other benefits from mutual connections and relationships with market partners like improving access to market information, strengthening market position and increasing the flexibility of business activity.
 Findings: The results suggest that in the case of enterprises operating in inter-organizational networks, better adaptation to customer needs is accompanied by strengthening the market position and providing better access to market information; however, it does not necessarily lead to greater flexibility of business activities.
 Research limitations/implications: A clear implication of the theoretical assumptions and conducted research is that although it is believed that in the case of enterprises operating in inter-organizational networks, better adaptation to customer needs leads to greater flexibility of operations in exceptional situations, for example, in micro-entities, where the ability to current settlement of liabilities and obtaining funds is limited, there will not necessarily be an increase in the flexibility of their business, which, however, does not reduce the possibility of shaping their social responsibility. 
 Practical implications: This study supports the current view that understanding customer needs shapes socially responsible enterprises operating in inter-organizational networks in terms of strengthening market position and improving access to market information. Moreover, the multi-aspect nature of understanding customer needs in the context of shaping corporate social responsibility and the interdisciplinary nature of the considerations create grounds for further research and exploration in this area. 
Originality/value: By focusing on the synergy of benefits generated by cooperation in inter organizational networks, the article contributes to research on understanding how mutual connections and relationships with market partners allow for adaptation to customer needs that may shape corporate social responsibility. (original abstract)

results.title: HRM Interventions in SMEs during the Covid-19 Pandemic Crisis

journal.title: Zeszyty Naukowe Politechniki Śląskiej. Seria Organizacja i Zarządzanie

abstracts.content:
Purpose: The purpose of this article is to present HRM interventions undertaken by SMEs during the crisis caused by the COVID-19 coronavirus. The research was conducted in 2021, following a critical moment of the crisis, which was expressed by a decrease in the incidence of the disease and the easing of restrictions introduced at the beginning of the pandemic. 
 Research design: The exploratory research was conducted on a sample of 200 companies. The surveyed companies were from south-eastern Poland, from the voivodeships of Silesia, Lesser Poland and Subcarpathia. Material for the analysis was obtained through semi-structured telephone interviews with their owners or managers. Descriptive statistics and a Chi-square test were used to analyze the data due to the qualitative nature of the variables. 
 Findings: The COVID-19 pandemic had a varied impact on the operations of the surveyed SMEs. Among the solutions introduced to cope with the pandemic challenges were reducing the scope/complexity of tasks, introducing crisis management solutions, or limiting the company's activities. In the area of people management, the examined companies made changes to their work organization, undertook activities aimed at supporting employees, and actions aimed at reducing labor costs. The measures taken were aimed, on the one hand, at ensuring the company's survival and, on the other hand, at creating conditions to maintain the current state of employment. 
 Research limitations/implications: The selection of 3 regions took into account the share of active SMEs in relation to the total number of SMEs in Poland. This made the research sample representative. Nevertheless, the diversity of companies belonging to the SMEs sector justifies the need for further research on both their experiences during the pandemic and its impact on the functioning of SMEs in the new post-pandemic reality. 
 Value: The results presented in the article contribute to the still limited knowledge of HRM in SMEs under crisis conditions, especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. (original abstract)
